You are an expert statistical plot illustrator. Write code to generate high-quality statistical plots based on user requests.

Use R with ggplot2 to generate a statistical plot based on the following detailed description: # Figure Description: `fig_intercept_error`

## Title and caption

- **Title:** Recorded Mean Squared Error at Three Intercept Corrections
- **Caption:** One deterministic calculation evaluated on the same five observations used to determine the correction (b = 3). No stochastic repetitions, optimizer, external dataset, held-out evaluation, uncertainty intervals, or interpolated/extrapolated values are shown.

## Content: variable mapping

- **x-axis:** intercept correction *b*, continuous, label "Intercept correction b".
- **y-axis:** mean squared error (MSE), continuous, label "Mean squared error (MSE)".
- **Visual channels:** position only. There is no hue, shape, or size mapping, since the figure has one series.
- **Geometry:** scatter points only. No connecting line, fitted curve, ribbon, or error bar.

## Complete list of plotted points

| # | b (x) | MSE (y) | Label above point | Source row in log |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 0 | 9 | "9" | Added b = 0 (MAE 3, MSE 9) |
| 2 | 1.5 | 2.25 | "2.25" | Added b = 1.5 (MAE 1.5, MSE 2.25) |
| 3 | 3 | 0 | "0" | Added b = 3 (MAE 0, MSE 0) |

Only these three pairs are drawn. The five (x, y) observations appear in the caption and the log, not on the plot.

## Presentation

**Canvas**
- Size: 5.0 in × 3.5 in, for a single-column manuscript figure.
- Background: white (`#FFFFFF`). No plot border.
- Font family: a single sans-serif family (Helvetica or Arial, falling back to the system sans) for all text, so the figure matches the manuscript body in embedded PDF output.
- Margins: default ggplot margins, with enough top room for the title and bottom room for the wrapped caption so neither is clipped.

**Axes**
- x-limits: [-0.25, 3.25]; breaks at 0, 1.5, 3.
- y-limits: [-0.5, 10]; breaks at 0, 3, 6, 9.
- Axis lines: `#222222`, 0.4 pt linewidth, drawn on the left and bottom edges only.
- Tick marks: `#222222`, 0.4 pt, length 2.5 pt, outward.
- Tick labels: 10 pt, `#222222`.
- Axis titles: 12 pt, `#222222`.

**Title**
- 13 pt, bold, `#222222`, left-aligned at the panel edge.
- Caption: 9 pt, italic, `#555555`, below the plot, left-aligned and wrapped to the figure width (5.0 in).

**Markers**
- Shape 16 (filled circle), size 3.2 mm diameter (about 9 pt).
- Fill and stroke: `#1F4E79`.

**Value labels**
- Text: "9", "2.25", "0", placed 0.5 data units above each point, so the label for b = 0 sits at y = 9.5 and stays inside the y-limit of 10.
- Font: 10 pt, regular, `#1F4E79`.

**Grid**
- Major horizontal gridlines only: `#D9D9D9`, 0.3 pt linewidth.
- No vertical gridlines.
- No minor gridlines.

**Legend**
- None. A legend is unnecessary for one series, so `legend.position = "none"`.

## Reproducibility code (R / ggplot2)

```r
library(ggplot2)

df <- data.frame(
  b   = c(0, 1.5, 3),
  mse = c(9, 2.25, 0),
  lab = c("9", "2.25", "0")
)

p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = b, y = mse)) +
  geom_point(shape = 16, size = 3.2, colour = "#1F4E79") +
  geom_text(aes(label = lab), nudge_y = 0.5, size = 3.5,
            colour = "#1F4E79", family = "sans") +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Intercept correction b",
                     breaks = c(0, 1.5, 3), limits = c(-0.25, 3.25)) +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Mean squared error (MSE)",
                     breaks = c(0, 3, 6, 9), limits = c(-0.5, 10)) +
  labs(title = "Recorded Mean Squared Error at Three Intercept Corrections",
       caption = paste("One deterministic calculation evaluated on the same",
                       "five observations used to determine the correction (b = 3).")) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10, base_family = "sans") +
  theme(
    plot.title         = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold", colour = "#222222", hjust = 0),
    plot.caption       = element_text(size = 9, face = "italic", colour = "#555555", hjust = 0),
    axis.title         = element_text(size = 12, colour = "#222222"),
    axis.text          = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#222222"),
    axis.line          = element_line(linewidth = 0.4, colour = "#222222"),
    axis.ticks         = element_line(linewidth = 0.4, colour = "#222222"),
    axis.ticks.length  = unit(2.5, "pt"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linewidth = 0.3, colour = "#D9D9D9"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    legend.position    = "none",
    plot.background    = element_rect(fill = "#FFFFFF", colour = NA)
  )

# Downstream artifacts: editable source, vector PDF, manuscript-compatible preview
ggsave("fig_intercept_error.pdf", p, device = cairo_pdf, width = 5, height = 3.5)
ggsave("fig_intercept_error.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5, dpi = 300)
```

## Choices I made

- Chose a single blue (`#1F4E79`) for points and labels, and neutral grays for structure, for a restrained scientific look. The blue-gray pairing stays distinguishable under common color-vision deficiencies, and the figure remains readable in grayscale.
- Chose horizontal gridlines only, so the reader can compare MSE levels without clutter.
- Set the x-range slightly beyond the data so the markers at b = 0 and b = 3 are not clipped.
- Set one sans-serif family throughout, so the text in the vector PDF matches the manuscript body.
